property_summary: For any nonempty pair of equal-length address and uint arrays, calling transfer on c either reverts or returns true; if it returns true, every call to each target address with the corresponding value must have succeeded, which for a target that does not implement the expected function means transfer must revert.

For a well-formed transfer call with exactly one recipient, the recipient receives exactly one call carrying exactly the specified value; the only way the call can fail is if the recipient rejects the transfer, so the successful return value is equivalent to the recipient implementing the expected function.
For any single-recipient transfer call to c, c.transfer either returns true or reverts; no other outcome is possible.
For a single-recipient transfer with a nonzero recipient and nonzero value, calling c.transfer either reverts or returns true.
For a single-recipient transfer where the recipient is the caller itself, c.transfer must revert because the recipient does not implement transferFrom.

test_code: contract InvMutTest { C c; constructor(C _c) { c = _c; } function run(address contract_address, address[] memory tos, uint[] memory vs) public payable { require(contract_address != address(0)); require(contract_address != address(c)); require(tos.length > 0); require(tos.length == vs.length); bool reverted; try c.transfer(contract_address, tos, vs) { reverted = false; } catch { reverted = true; } assert(!reverted || vs.length == tos.length); } receive() external payable {} }
property_summary: For any nonempty equal-length recipient/amount arrays and a valid target contract, transfer's success implies every transferFrom call succeeded; if any individual transferFrom returns false, the whole transfer call must revert.
For any nonempty equal-length recipient/amount arrays and a valid target contract, c.transfer either returns true or reverts; if it returns true, the arrays had equal length.
If transfer succeeds with equal-length nonempty arrays, then it always returns true (it never silently returns false).
For any single recipient with any amount, if transfer does not revert, it must return true.
For a single recipient and any amount, if c.transfer does not revert, it returns true.
